characters.name: Maren Pike
characters.goal: complete shift handover and go home to sleep

characters.name: Arthur Orde
characters.goal: inspect the rush dockyard glaze batch immediately

characters.name: Tilda Keel
characters.goal: avoid getting drawn into management trouble

characters.name: Foster Vance
characters.goal: finish his maintenance tea break in peace

characters.name: Moran Teague
characters.goal: shield union members from disciplinary action

objects.name: Night Shift Logbook
objects.status: bound in blue cloth on desk

premise.logline: A glaze factory kiln is opened a day early and a worker is found inside, and the shift supervisor who holds the only key has to account for a night she cannot remember clearly.

modules.theme: how a workplace decides in advance who will be blamed
modules.setting_time: a winter of short shifts and a failing order book
modules.setting_place: a glaze works on the edge of a port town
modules.protagonist: the night shift supervisor, recently promoted from the floor
modules.protagonist_want: to reconstruct a night she spent too tired to remember properly
modules.antagonism: a management that has already chosen its account of events
modules.complication: her own reconstruction keeps producing a version that convicts her
modules.ending_shape: the truth is established and costs the person who established it

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

events.summary: Works manager Arthur Orde arrives at dawn demanding the early opening of Kiln 4 to salvage the dockyard order.
events.dramatic_function: Establish the protagonist's exhaustion, the management pressure, and the early kiln opening.
beats: Orde interrupts Maren as she attempts to sign out after a grueling sixteen-hour double shift.
Orde insists that Kiln 4 must be unsealed twenty-four hours early because the naval dockyard order will be canceled if not shipped today.
Maren checks her pocket and confirms the single brass master key is in her sole possession.

state_changes.value: account for the night shift to Orde

events.summary: Maren unlocks Kiln 4 on Orde's orders and discovers the body of kiln loader Gabe Callow inside.
events.dramatic_function: The inciting disturbance: an impossible workplace fatality inside a locked chamber.
beats: Maren unlocks the heavy muffle door clamps using the brass master key while Tilda assists with the winch.
The kiln door swings outward, revealing Gabe Callow collapsed lifelessly across the lower tier of glaze plaques.
Orde immediately blocks Tilda from approaching the chamber and shouts for the factory alarm.

events.summary: Orde publicly blames Maren for locking the kiln without checking the interior, citing her sole key custody.
events.dramatic_function: Establish the management narrative: pinning the death onto the exhausted junior supervisor.
beats: Orde demands to know how a man was locked inside a muffle kiln when Maren carries the only key.
Maren struggles through a fog of exhaustion to recall sealing the door at two in the morning.
Tilda watches silently as Orde announces that the shift log records Maren's own signature sealing the chamber.

state_changes.value: pin responsibility for Gabe's death on Maren

events.summary: In the works office, Orde suspends Maren and prepares an official negligence report against her.
events.dramatic_function: Lock the protagonist into the investigator role by threatening her freedom and career.
beats: Orde confiscates Maren's supervisor badge and instructs her to leave the premises before the town coroner arrives.
Maren objects that she cannot remember turning the bolt while Gabe was missing from the floor.
Orde warns her that the board will treat her fatigue as gross personal negligence rather than an institutional failure.

state_changes.value: reconstruct the night shift timeline to clear herself

events.summary: Maren questions yardman Foster Vance about the metallic pounding she vaguely remembers hearing during the night.
events.dramatic_function: Plant the explanation for the noise Maren mistook for Gabe banging from inside the kiln.
beats: Maren slips into the mill canteen and confronts Foster over his tea.
Foster admits he was up on the flue catwalk at two in the morning hammering out a jammed damper lever.
Foster complains that the plant's cut-rate maintenance has left every flue vibrating like an iron drum.

events.summary: Chemist Nel Scurlock shows Maren that the pyrometric cones from Kiln 4 did not deform until hours after two in the morning.
events.dramatic_function: Introduce physical evidence proving the firing cycle did not begin when Maren supposedly sealed the kiln.
beats: Maren visits Nel in the glaze laboratory to inspect the test cones pulled from Kiln 4's sight-hole.
Nel demonstrates that Cone 04 did not bend until four in the morning, indicating the heat rise was delayed by hours.
Nel observes dispassionately that someone altered the normal automated gas cycle.

events.summary: Maren returns to the shift office to examine her blue logbook and finds Gabe's personal brass tally tag pinned to her desk.
events.dramatic_function: Deepen Maren's internal doubt by showing physical traces that suggest she was present during Gabe's check-in.
beats: Maren re-enters the vacant supervisor office and inspects the blue hardbound shift log.
She confirms the 02:00 entry reading 'Kiln 4 sealed and dog-latched' is unmistakably in her own handwriting.
Beside the logbook, she finds Gabe's numbered brass tally tag resting on her blotter, where only she could have placed it.

events.summary: Maren corners Tilda Keel, who admits she saw Maren slumped completely unconscious in the office around three in the morning.
events.dramatic_function: Plant the witness testimony establishing Maren's period of total blackout.
beats: Maren finds Tilda sweeping spilled grog on the cooling floor and presses her for what she saw during the night.
Tilda tearfully admits she looked through the office window at 03:00 and saw Maren dead asleep across her desk.
Tilda refuses to speak further, terrified that Orde will revoke her seasonal contract.

events.summary: Nel helps Maren examine the brass master key under magnification and identifies wet red iron oxide slip on the handle.
events.dramatic_function: Plant an obscure forensic detail that will later connect Orde to the key theft.
beats: Maren brings the brass master key to the lab for Nel to inspect for forced ward marks.
Nel finds no scratches on the wards but discovers a dried smear of red iron oxide slip on the brass bow.
Nel remarks that the red slip was only used for the experimental dockyard plaques, which Gabe was not assigned to mix.

events.summary: Union steward Moran Teague warns Maren that the union will not defend a junior supervisor if it risks floor workers' jobs.
events.dramatic_function: Reinforce the theme: the workplace closing ranks against the appointed scapegoat.
beats: Moran stops Maren by the tea urn and tells her the union committee met informally.
Moran explains that management has offered to protect seasonal shop jobs if the fatality is logged as supervisory error.
He bluntly advises Maren to accept an administrative dismissal rather than trigger a criminal inquest.

state_changes.value: force Maren to accept individual fault

events.summary: Maren discovers the gas pressure barograph chart stuffed beneath the filing cabinet in the supervisor's office.
events.dramatic_function: Uncover the instrument record documenting the exact time the kiln burners ignited.
beats: Maren searches the supervisor office for mechanical records and spots paper wedged under the cabinet base.
She retrieves the circular barograph chart recording gas pressure for Kiln 4.
The inked needle shows pressure remained flat until 03:45, when an abrupt high-pressure spike was initiated.

events.summary: Combining the barograph spike with her memory gaps, Maren concludes she sleepwalked or woke delirious at 03:45 and fired the kiln herself.
events.dramatic_function: The Wrong Turn: a coherent, defensible reading of the evidence that convinces Maren of her own guilt.
beats: Maren correlates the pyrometric cone delay with the 03:45 barograph gas surge.
She assumes that in her severe exhaustion, she must have woken confused, seen the low flame, turned the valve, and relocked the door.
Overcome with horror, Maren concludes that she herself killed Gabe through sleep-deprived delirium.

state_changes.value: face the reality of her own fatal mistake

events.summary: Maren confides her self-incriminating deduction to Moran, who urges her to sign an internal resignation before the police board arrives.
events.dramatic_function: Deepen the trap by showing the union eager to validate Maren's false confession.
beats: Maren tells Moran in the canteen that she believes she relit the burners at 03:45 while half-asleep.
Moran seizes on her admission, telling her that signing a voluntary resignation will keep the matter out of the assize courts.
He escorts her directly toward the management office to put an end to the inquiry.

events.summary: Maren meets Orde in the works office to sign the indemnity statement, but hesitates over the exact wording.
events.dramatic_function: Bring the protagonist to the brink of formal self-destruction before the truth breaks.
beats: Orde places a drafted statement on the mahogany desk admitting total supervisor oversight.
He hands Maren a fountain pen, assuring her that the firm will quietly settle Gabe's family pension.
Maren leans forward to sign, her pen hovering over the paper.

state_changes.value: secure Maren's signed confession before the board convenes

events.summary: Maren spots red slip on Orde's sleeve and a 03:30 dockyard rush docket on his desk, shattering her false confession.
events.dramatic_function: The collapse of the Wrong Turn: Maren recognizes that Orde handled the red slip and was on the floor at 03:30.
beats: As Maren reaches for the paper, she notices a smear of dried red iron oxide slip on Orde's right shirt cuff.
She sees an internal dockyard rush docket dated 03:30 in Orde's desk organizer, approving high-fire cure.
Maren drops the pen, realizing that the red slip on her key matches Orde's cuff, not her own hands.

state_changes.value: prove Orde entered the kiln after she fell asleep

events.summary: Maren confronts Tilda in the glaze lab alongside Nel, forcing Tilda to admit that Gabe was alive at 03:15 when Orde ordered him into the kiln.
events.dramatic_function: Provide the vital witness breakthrough of the Solution phase.
beats: Maren brings Tilda into the lab and confronts her with the chemical evidence and the 03:30 docket.
Under Nel's quiet scrutiny, Tilda breaks down and confesses she was having tea with Gabe at 03:15.
Tilda reveals that Orde entered the canteen at 03:20 and ordered Gabe back into Kiln 4 to reset fallen saggers before the rush fire.

state_changes.value: tell the truth about Gabe's final orders

events.summary: In the shift office, Maren reconstructs how Orde stole the key from her pocket while she slept, locked Gabe inside, and returned the key.
events.dramatic_function: The synthesis beat of the Solution phase: assembling the full true sequence of events.
beats: Foster confirms that while he was repairing the damper at 02:15, Maren was already stumbling with exhaustion.
Maren pieces together how Orde entered the office while she was unconscious at 03:30, slipped the key from her coat, and went to Kiln 4.
Nel notes that Orde must have started the high-pressure gas at 03:45 without realizing Gabe was still in the back flue, then returned the key to Maren's pocket.

events.summary: Maren, Nel, and Moran confront Orde in his office with the timeline, the red slip stains, and the pyrometric evidence.
events.dramatic_function: Deliver the climax of the Solution phase: the truth is demonstrated beyond dispute.
beats: Maren presents the red slip traces, the 03:30 rush docket, and Tilda's statement directly before Moran.
Nel confirms that the thermal delay matches the gas barograph spike initiated under Orde's dockyard authority.
Cornered by the evidence, Orde breaks his silence and admits he locked the dog-latch thinking Gabe had already exited through the side wicket.

events.summary: The works management and the union agree to a quiet settlement: Orde is granted early retirement while the night shift is permanently eliminated.
events.dramatic_function: The Cost phase begins: institutional power realigns to protect the institution rather than justice.
beats: Moran and Orde negotiate an institutional compromise behind closed doors to prevent police charges that would close the works.
Orde is permitted to resign with full pension on medical grounds, logging Gabe's death as an unavoidable industrial accident.
Moran announces that to satisfy the board's insurance underwriters, the entire night shift roster will be dissolved.

state_changes.value: seal the institutional compromise to keep the plant open

events.summary: Maren collects her coat from the canteen, knowing she has established the truth but is permanently blacklisted from the port's glaze works.
events.dramatic_function: The final Cost: the whistleblower is cleared of manslaughter but stripped of her livelihood and community.
beats: Maren cleans out her locker while Tilda watches from the doorway in ashamed silence.
Tilda tells Maren that word has already spread among the port manufacturers that Maren is dangerous to employ.
Maren walks out into the port town winter dusk, her name legally clear and her working life over.

state_changes.value: leave the port town with her name intact
